0.long_answer: The fish known as 'the fish that inebriates' in the Indo-Pacific region is Mulloidichthys flavolineatus. This species is among those that have been reported to produce hallucinogenic effects when consumed, likely because of the toxins or compounds it accumulates from its diet. Found in coral reefs and rocky coastal habitats from East Africa to Hawaii, it is one of the several species associated with ichthyoallyeinotoxism, a condition where eating the fish results in intoxication or delirious effects. Although other fish, such as Sarpa salpa, are also noted for similar effects, Sarpa salpa is native to the Mediterranean and adjacent waters, whereas Mulloidichthys flavolineatus is characteristic of the Indo-Pacific region.
